decisions.reason: The project has explicit domain owners. Global event buses, new autoloads, editor plugins and node-per-entity migration add unnecessary lifecycle and invalidation obligations.

clock_decision_review.trigger: The user explicitly relaxed shared-clock alignment and selected independent event/timer progression while either view is hidden.
clock_decision_review.requirement: Both domains progress while hidden through their own owned events/timers and active physical work. Preserve explicit pause/speed intent and local/causal ordering; equal domain clocks and world-wide advancement are not required. E14 is the active requirement.

retirement_target.scope: Remove the live world-wide scheduling/reconciliation role of game/staffing/rear_simulation.gd::advance_time and its global _settle loop after responsibility-by-responsibility migration.
retirement_target.replacement: Persistent local lifecycle owners drive affected work and discrete deadlines. A narrow custody coordinator handles causal transfer handoffs. Views bind to committed revisions; navigation does not advance or align domain clocks.
retirement_target.architecture_gate: A new service must not require another entry in world-wide next-boundary, advance and settlement lists. Do not rename the same all-service dispatcher or move it wholesale into _process.
retirement_target.time_source_choice: Prefer native engine mechanisms for each suitable local activity; no separate custom shared world clock is required. Timer pause/speed integration, short-deadline precision and local tie order must pass EV03/R29 before rollout. Keep current common user controls without treating local timestamps as interchangeable.
retirement_target.helpers: Small domain update/step methods, ledger clock helpers and explicit-time test adapters may remain. They must not recreate a second authority or the retired global polling loop.
retirement_target.migration_gate: Keep each responsibility under exactly one active driver. Preserve required ordering, no-UI behavior, physical safety, elapsed work and cancellation before disconnecting its legacy path.
retirement_target.caller_gate: Inventory live, test, fixture and retained-demo callers. Migrate or explicitly adapt them; do not silently break retained consumers or hide the old implementation in ignored support code.
retirement_target.initial_slice: S01/S02 still leave the existing driver intact to isolate read/UI changes. That is a temporary staging constraint, not the final architecture.

coupling_review.evidence_scope: Original structural coupling findings are retained. E13 refreshes current anchors and adds a bounded scene-owned live process-frame guard; advance_time policy and settlement order remain. _settle adds opt-in inclusive timing only. Runtime passes are separately bounded in the E13 evidence.
coupling_review.boundary_count_meaning: 18 conditional service next_boundary call sites, plus yard, production activities, actors and job aging. This is static structure, not a per-second frequency or proof all work is redundant.

consequences.observation: A boundary in one service divides the global interval; each segment enumerates other service boundaries and is followed by broad settlement. Settlement repeats its service/actor/store checks when anything reports a change.
consequences.impact: One activity's boundaries can increase unrelated reevaluation; cost grows with both world size and boundary frequency.
consequences.limit: The 1000 settlement iterations are a convergence cap, not a claim that every invocation runs 1000 passes. CPU attribution and representative performance measurements remain required.

consequences.observation: Accrual, actor movement, individual advance_to calls, ledger/rear clock changes and settlement occur in a fixed code order. More than one service can participate in the same completion/handoff.
consequences.impact: Moving one service to an independent callback can alter which state another sees at a boundary. Required ordering must become a documented service/transition contract.
consequences.limit: This identifies migration risk; it does not establish a current ordering bug.

consequences.observation: The UI defaults untagged legacy results to reconciliation. Explicit read-only Training rejections now bypass deferred session notification and after_command while retaining local feedback/refresh. Accepted Training and other legacy non-speed/non-inspection results still invoke after_command; in the live-planning branch it invalidates planning and calls advance_time(0.0,true), which settles before checking elapsed time.
consequences.impact: Read-only Training rejection no longer performs global reconciliation. Accepted/no-op/other-service commands still require individual mutation-contract characterization before removing legacy guarantees.
consequences.limit: Not every result follows this branch, and not every command is proven to duplicate work. Record actual command reasons/counts before removing existing guarantees.
consequences.baseline_observation: Except for tagged speed/inspection results, the UI result path invokes after_command. In the live-planning branch it invalidates route planning and calls advance_time(0.0,true); advance_time settles before checking the elapsed interval.

consequences.observation: Session time/state notifications still reach both views. Rear refresh deduplicates only while pending; normal Build/Supplies/Workers/Train use narrow branches. Other advanced panels and HQ diagnostics still enter broad snapshots.
consequences.impact: World progression can fan out into repeated presentation reads even when much displayed information is unchanged.
consequences.limit: Expensive UI exports are a distinct read-path problem. Retiring the dispatcher alone does not fix them; prior inspect_entity call shares are not CPU shares.
consequences.followup: E13 coalesces background wall-clock pumps per process frame; UI refresh remains deduplicated while pending, not guaranteed once per frame. Existing command/explicit-time paths retain their own semantics.

consequences.observation: The world driver names domain services and their boundary/advance/settle interfaces individually.
consequences.impact: Adding or migrating a service requires updating central orchestration and understanding unrelated settlement side effects. A service cannot fully own its lifecycle while the global driver remains responsible for its progress and reconciliation.
consequences.limit: Shared coordination for a real physical transaction may remain appropriate; the target is to remove all-service knowledge and polling rather than prohibit every coordinator.

coupling_review.target_decision: Phase out the live world-wide advance_time/_settle dispatcher through verified service migrations. This is a planned architectural decision; implementation choices and measured performance remain unproven.
coupling_review.E15_anchor_epoch_note: Previous anchors retain the actual before-change source snapshot used in logs/gdunit4-performance-2026-11-04T14-07-15-22564; each of these eight method bodies is unchanged, while BaseDemo source lines/file fingerprint shifted.

current_source_observations: GameSession remains physics-callback driven; E13 permits one pump per engine process frame only for already wall-clock-driven live models. Explicit-delta models still receive every physics step.
Live tick_live accrues the full Time.get_ticks_usec interval on the next permitted pump; set_speed accrues the preceding interval before changing the speed policy.
BaseSimulation still owns owed simulation time and bounded planning/advance quanta. RearSimulation.advance_time still scans service boundaries, accrues work, moves actors and runs global settlement.
E13 removes repeated detailed cohesion/member and unused mounted/rack exports without deferring immediate safety or changing recipes, opening, engine rates or performance limits.

native_alternative.candidate: Use _physics_process(delta) for appropriate continuous physical updates and engine-driven callbacks, active processing or Timers for relevant activities. Domain services may remain lightweight models delegated to by scene-owned Nodes.
native_alternative.speed: Existing Pause/1x/2x controls remain the default UX across local drivers. A deliberate engine-time-scale migration is possible but must not double-scale work or UI timing. Independent per-area controls are not introduced by this revision.
native_alternative.pause: SceneTree.paused plus process modes can stop gameplay while UI and pure planning continue. Pause capability alone does not justify a custom clock.
native_alternative.domain_steps: Small update/step methods remain useful for pure domain tests and reuse. Testing such methods does not require the whole current world-clock/settlement architecture.
risks_to_characterize: Independent callback order must preserve required arrival, earned-work, cancellation and same-time completion behavior.
Global engine time scaling can affect UI delta-based animations/timers as well as gameplay; diagnostics and watchdogs must retain real-second meaning.
Rendering hitches, physics catch-up limits, paused commands and pending route preparation can produce different outcomes under a new timing policy.
Moving the same broad scans into _process does not remove their work. Active subscriptions/processing and narrow reads remain separate optimization tasks.

Keep it unchanged for S01/S02 so read/UI work can be compared in isolation, then retire its migrated responsibilities progressively. acceptance: Equivalent legal state transitions, physical handoffs, admission/consumption and exactly-once completion.
Pause, 1x/2x, staff/access changes, cancellation at a completion boundary, hitches and session replacement retain their intended behavior.
Tests can exercise domain rules without requiring wall-clock minutes to elapse.
Measure CPU/frame behavior and compare implementation complexity/ownership. Retain only clock/deadline machinery whose benefit is evidenced.
R25-R32 add independent hidden progression, explicit transfer custody and final-pose placement gates; no cross-domain equal-clock outcome is required.

sources.title: Head First Design Patterns, Second Edition

refinements.application: Use scoped Godot signals for facts that have committed, then invalidate affected views/services. Preserve immediate safety callbacks and explicit subscriber ownership.
refinements.clarification: Notification alone does not make an arbitrary UI query cheap, detach its data, guarantee one refresh per frame or perform safe lifecycle rebinding. Those remain explicit project responsibilities.
refinements.planned_gate: Each notification names its producer, committed facts/IDs, subscribers, teardown policy and delivery class; prove zero commands during view synchronization and no lost dirty IDs.

refinements.application: Give a user intent one validated domain entry and one reconciliation result. Record action/target/session IDs, acceptance and actual mutation/revision so UI receipts connect to the resulting game outcome.
refinements.representation: An ordinary typed method/result is sufficient until queued requests, replay or another concrete requirement justifies a command object. This is not a new framework requirement.
refinements.cancellation: Cancellation remains a domain operation with its own physical/refund rules. A generic undo command must not recreate consumed materials, delivered people or completed outputs.
refinements.planned_gate: One input causes one intended domain command; rejected/no-op requests do not claim a mutation, and accepted commands retain their documented reconciliation and conservation behavior.

refinements.application: Before migrating an activity's driver, write its legal state transitions, guards and effects. First characterize current training presentation normalization; later distinguish canonical job state from derived display reasons.
refinements.representation: Choose enums, a transition table or separate state objects according to the real behavior variation and complexity. The book's state classes are an option rather than a requirement for every row or job.
refinements.planned_gate: Exercise legal and rejected transitions, cancelled/completed terminal behavior and equal-time interruption; qualification/output/consumption effects occur exactly once.

refinements.application: Keep tightly related rules with their actual owner. Declare the permitted read/command/notification boundary for each migrated slice so UI or another service does not gain a second authority.
refinements.status_policy: A selected architectural direction is not an implemented or passing result. Retain both decision status and implementation/evidence status.
refinements.planned_gate: Expand the affected A01-A05 decision into a record when its implementation slice starts; link the state owner, regressions, measurements and rollback. Avoid creating records for trivial local edits.

refinements.application: Use representative states and repeated comparable runs; report spread and tail behavior as well as central values. Apply uncertainty methods only when their sampling assumptions fit the actual measurements.
refinements.project_inference: Successive game frames share scene state, queued work and operating-system conditions. Frame count must not be presented as the same number of independent benchmark repetitions. This is an application of sampling principles to this project, not a claim the book specifically analyzes Godot frames.
refinements.planned_gate: Record per-run distributions, sample counts, warm-up, run order and comparable logical work. Define the percentile calculation and regression tolerance before comparing implementations; report inconclusive evidence when variation overwhelms the observed change.

refinements.application: Apply a pattern to a named dependency, transition or action problem and choose a representation suited to GDScript and current ownership.
refinements.project_judgment: The references do not by themselves establish a performance improvement, prescribe a Node per record, justify a new global bus, or require separate classes for every action/state.
refinements.planned_gate: Every additional abstraction states the concrete problem, ownership/lifecycle cost and expected benefit; compare behavior and measured work before expanding its use.

reference_refinements.verification_limits: No new game implementation or runtime measurement was performed for this book review. The previously recorded nine domain-test passes and five open timing violations retain their original scope and status.
reference_refinements.sequence_note_E14: Original section review/history is retained. E13 bounded fixes are implemented; E14 migration_contracts now refines the next delivery sequence and removes the shared-clock constraint. No new book review or architecture benchmark was executed.

New game/model replacement during pending refresh, deferred scroll restoration, confirmation and route work; destroy or detach views before callback. Old valid objects/generations cannot write to the new session. Disconnect surviving subscribers and reconnect once.

Mutate nested arrays/dictionaries in returned view and selected detail; authority and a second independent view remain unchanged. Cover Resource references if introduced; read-only outer container alone is insufficient.

Inventory all legacy exports removed by panel narrowing. Detect writes/signals/raw owner state changes and classify necessary normalization. Compare independent fixtures with/without UI reads; do not make necessary game behavior disappear when hidden exports stop running.

Two different IDs and different changes in the same frame both survive deduplication; dirtied-during-drain work is retained. Check insert/delete/transfer/split/merge, holder ancestry/mass, reservation changes, health/fuel/crew/assignment and failed/rolled-back transactions against canonical scans.

Pause stops authoritative time/movement/earned work while legal commands and pure planning remain usable. Switch 1x/2x/pause mid-job; custom clock and engine timers obey explicit policy. Compare domain outcomes at equal logical times, recording wall-time debt.
regression_matrix.E14_scope_clarification: Apply to each local owner and required causal/physical ordering; cross-domain absolute time equality is no longer a requirement. Historical global-clock fixtures remain recorded and require deliberate adapters.

regression_matrix.check: Coarse/partitioned explicit advances and multiple physics steps per render agree on required normalized outcomes. Test deadline exactly at cancel/access/staff/rate change, large hitch, duplicate deadline and changed-then-restored state. No job strands because a wakeup was dropped.
regression_matrix.E14_scope_clarification: Apply to each local owner and required causal/physical ordering; cross-domain absolute time equality is no longer a requirement. Historical global-clock fixtures remain recorded and require deliberate adapters.

regression_matrix.check: Rerun all 11 facilities in two orientations, rejected placement, started cancellation and completed rejection. Add partially delivered M11, haul/carry in flight, first-work consumption boundary, safe return haul, retired/occupied facilities and selection across cancellation; conserve materials and release capacity once.

Canonical identity/custody/stock/fuel/gear/ammunition, rear population/fleet places, bay/parking capacity and incoming reservations balance before/after success/reject/cancel/death. A claim is not delivery or physical movement.

Continuous contact/damage/wreck consequences precede further movement. Route changes invalidate stale plans; fuel is charged for real distance. Indexes and observers preserve ownership and observed-versus-physical enemy knowledge.

Legacy and migrated code never complete the same responsibility. Job/session generation rejects cancelled/replaced work; exactly one output, refund/consumption rule and reservation release. Explicit-time fixture driver remains available or is deliberately migrated.

Use native rendered runs for buttons/popup/options, keyboard/focus and small-window layouts. Verify viewport coordinate transforms at supported scaling. Headless runs do not certify native menus or pixel hit targets.

Repeat create/show/hide/replace/free cycles; no rising live node/reference count, orphan work, duplicate subscriptions or closures retaining old models. RefCounted cycles and deferred-deletion lifetime are checked explicitly.

Use performance_protocol below, record CPU self/total, frame and refresh percentiles, logical-time progress, counts and instrumentation mode. Improvement must be in matched states without lower simulation work or changed visual cadence.

Default first issue pauses with logs, unique stacks, last input, raw/checkpoint state, screenshot and pending tests. Audit mode may continue with each issue retained. Retained-domain selections must appear explicitly in manifest; never equate source reachability/call count with executed coverage.

Requery map and reread actual functions before edits; refresh inventory drift where relevant. Update map -> UI diagram/button manifest -> map, review every changed function purpose against code and pass both --check tools with zero pending reviews.

Hold each observation view, then hide both for a prepared interval with active logistics jobs, battlefield movement/combat and a shipment. Compare against equivalent fixtures with no navigation. Both owners complete expected local work; switch timing cannot change outcomes. No duplicated full model or frozen hidden-domain state.

For every migrated activity, enumerate each blocking dependency and change it while the view is hidden, paused, or in transition. Prove exactly the affected jobs wake and liveness survives changed-then-restored state, rate/assignment/access changes, duplicate notifications and finite reentrant batches. Idle/blocked jobs perform no repeated eligibility scan.

Use real prepared hull/cargo/crew. Exercise timer ready, blocked entry, berth/capacity release, physical approach, partial unload, delivery, interruption/resume, cancellation, return, destruction and old/duplicate receipt. Timer expiry cannot credit supplies. Audit one hull/manifest custody, actual fuel and on-map hazards, exactly-once delivered portions and no handoff depending on navigation.

Rapidly alternate views during active transfers/work, at a commit, and around new session/close/reopen. Subscribe/read revision races preserve changes; selected IDs/focus remain valid. Old generations cannot publish, connections do not grow, hidden views avoid structural exports, and transition callbacks issue no game commands or world settlement.

regression_matrix.area: Local timer policy and tie boundaries
regression_matrix.check: Exercise Pause/1x/2x before/during countdown, rate/access/staff changes, timeout/cancel and arrival/damage ties, delayed frames, multiple physics steps per render, old callbacks and save/load rearming. Accrue prior-rate work, preserve remaining duration and required local order. Cross-domain transfer order is causal, without comparing unrelated absolute clocks or applying time scaling twice.

regression_matrix.area: Actual pointer placement and fresh commit
regression_matrix.check: Use native input: select every supported building/rotation, move to arbitrary valid/invalid/far-edge positions, rapid same-frame move-and-click, stationary hover while geometry changes, zoom/pan, paused input, Escape/right-click cancel, placement cancellation/dismantle with retained stock and repeated placements. Hover does not run full route/connectivity validation; click validates final authoritative pose and all existing access rules. Verify collider/ghost lifetime and world transforms.

partial_execution.limits: Independent drivers/timers and full 55-case/system acceptance are not covered. No Area2D performance benchmark. Vehicle-works cancellation still exceeds original limits.

regression_matrix.check: Repeat affected actual-game placement, independent/background progress, simultaneous completions, blocked-transfer release and view switching at 1x in warmed matched runs. Enforce the E16 1000/60 ms whole-frame and synchronous-action ceiling and retain the 30000 inspection/s diagnostic limit and existing 0.25 s placement time-debt assertion; measure each local domain progress/debt after migration. Record CPU attribution, p50/p95/p99/max, end-to-end actions, completed work, memory/timer/connection counts and actual work per real second. Counters and unique-stack attribution runs are separated. First performance/functional issue pauses the selected run and writes the existing logs artifacts; no limit increases, dropped simulation work or hidden failures.

partial_execution.limits: Independent drivers/timers and full 55-case/system acceptance are not covered. No Area2D performance benchmark. Vehicle-works cancellation still exceeds original limits.

regression_matrix.previous_check_before_E16: Repeat affected actual-game placement, independent/background progress, simultaneous completions, blocked-transfer release and view switching at 1x in warmed matched runs. Retain the current 100 ms frame/action and 30000 inspection/s limits and existing 0.25 s placement time-debt assertion; measure each local domain progress/debt after migration. Record CPU attribution, p50/p95/p99/max, end-to-end actions, completed work, memory/timer/connection counts and actual work per real second. Counters and unique-stack attribution runs are separated. First performance/functional issue pauses the selected run and writes the existing logs artifacts; no limit increases, dropped simulation work or hidden failures.
regression_matrix.active_target: E16 supersedes the prior severe-stall criterion; whole-game compliance remains false.

regression_matrix.area: Compatibility, source maps and coverage limits
regression_matrix.check: Keep E13 cohesion/mounted-read fixes, frozen original fixtures and current default opening/resources/pause intact. Run affected retained-domain and native suites, then the complete selected acceptance suite before declaring the overhaul complete. Adapt old shared-clock fixtures only against explicitly changed local/causal requirements and preserve their historical expectations. Inventory retained live/demo callers; no plugin startup dependency. Update map, UI flowchart and button manifest, review changed function purposes, and pass both checks. Report excluded, unprepared and unreached cases; no claim of testing every function.

partial_execution.limits: Independent drivers/timers and full 55-case/system acceptance are not covered. No Area2D performance benchmark. Vehicle-works cancellation still exceeds original limits.

regression_matrix.area: Hard 60 FPS acceptance and non-bypassable failure capture
regression_matrix.check: Exercise 17 ms frame/action rejection with real pause/log output; attempted 100 ms overrides cannot weaken the ceiling. Actual uncapped 1x native runs must satisfy every frame plus existing progress/correctness guards. Capture over-budget source/state; do not run final-pose input/assertions after pause.

performance_protocol.entry: Establish baseline variance before choosing a numerical regression tolerance; do not tune thresholds after seeing a failure.
matched_states: Normal playable empty-field Build at 1x as an already narrowed control.
Prepared populated Train at 1x with actual reporting/active/paused students and legal instructor coverage; record fixture/time/work.
The same prepared Train state with HQ diagnostics enabled, measured separately.
Pause and 2x correctness/control observations; matched 2x performance when a clock/scheduler slice is affected.
procedure: Run serially on the same engine, renderer, viewport, frame cap and source version; no imports/map generation or concurrent test project during measurement.

Initial screening protocol: three warmed 30-second observations per affected live scenario. Persist fixture inputs, logical start/end time, work completed and environment; record shorter action windows separately. Three runs are a starting screen, not a sample-size or statistical-confidence guarantee.
Time the normal path with diagnostics/stack capture off where possible; collect a counters-only run and a separate bounded stack-attribution run. Never compare stack-on before to stack-off after.

Use CPU profiler self and total time to distinguish exporter cost from caller fanout. Measure _refresh duration and end-to-end frame p50/p95/p99/max, action latency, logical-time debt and live planning progress.
Normalize counts by real second, logical second and UI refresh where relevant. A slower simulation or fewer visible updates cannot count as success.
Compare old/new on independent equivalent fixtures at matching logical times. Performance measurement must not call both implementations on one authority.

E16: record engine frame cap/VSync request and isolate intentional pacing from capacity; do not compare new uncapped input stress against old capped observations as an optimization speedup. Every over-budget frame remains a failure requiring attribution.
acceptance: No median/p95/p99 CPU or frame regression beyond the baseline noise/tolerance established before the change; inspect distributions and outliers rather than only average counts.
A read-split slice demonstrates removal of specified unrelated snapshot chains and a reproducible refresh/CPU improvement in its target scenario.

E16 user requirement: every measured native frame and synchronous action must remain within 1000/60 ms (16.666666666666668 ms). Averages/p95/p99 alone cannot pass a run with an observed over-budget frame. Use uncapped capacity measurements with VSync disabled by request and retain raw observations. The 30000 inspection/s diagnostic budget and correctness/progress guards remain; prior 100 ms passes are historical severe-stall evidence only.

Known timing failures remain open and visible. A slice may have bounded passing evidence while the full-suite result remains failing; never report the whole suite green or silently whitelist the five existing violations.

sampling_and_uncertainty.replication: Keep separately restarted matched runs as the replication unit. Preserve per-run data and account for run order, thermal/background drift and logical-time workload; do not assume every consecutive frame is an independent repetition.
sampling_and_uncertainty.comparison_order: Pair comparable old/new runs with reset fixtures and recorded inputs; alternate or randomize their order when practical to expose order/drift effects. Keep instrumentation modes identical within a comparison.
sampling_and_uncertainty.percentiles: Report per-run sample counts, observation duration, warm-up and the chosen quantile/interpolation convention consistently. Treat p99/max from short windows as descriptive; inspect raw stalls and add repeated runs when tails or between-run variation are unstable.
sampling_and_uncertainty.inference: Choose sample size and an uncertainty method appropriate to the chosen run-level metric and dependence assumptions before making confidence claims. Report practical effect size and inconclusive comparisons; three run means or thousands of correlated frames do not automatically justify a confidence interval.
sampling_and_uncertainty.decision: Functional failures and recorded severe stalls remain actionable even when an average improves. Never average away the five existing timing violations or compare unlike prepared states as a before/after result.

failure_artifacts: Input receipt and last action, session/job IDs and logical/wall time.
Per-second counts and unique call stacks in a separate attribution run.
Raw state and audited checkpoint, screenshot for native input, remaining/pending case list, engine errors.
prohibited_shortcuts: Increasing budgets to get a pass.
Changing default opening/recipe rates/physical speed or dropping time.
Reducing polling/visual cadence without an explicit separate behavior decision.
Updating frozen expected hashes to match a failed refactor.
Treating fewer inspect_entity calls as sufficient proof of lower CPU or correct outcomes.
Restore the old 100 ms target, use average FPS to hide isolated drops, or omit overshoots to label a run 60 FPS compliant.
performance_protocol.previous_severe_stall_acceptance_before_: The existing 100ms frame/action and 30000 inspections/s defaults remain severe-stall gates until deliberately revised. They are not a 16.67ms/60fps target; a user-facing frame target remains an explicit decision.

delivery_and_rollback.before_code: Record affected source hashes and current expected states, inspect existing user edits, and keep a small reviewable slice. No destructive reset of the shared workspace.
stop_conditions: Any new functional error, audit violation or mismatch.
Lost dirty ID, obsolete callback side effect or duplicate completion.
Timing/call-budget failure without attributed explanation and saved artifacts.
Performance improvement caused by reduced logical-time progress/work.
Necessary hidden query side effects cannot yet be safely owned.
delivery_and_rollback.action_on_failure: Pause the test by default, save evidence, restore only the current slice's routing or driver, and fix the failing case before advancing. Keep the characterization/test and known-failure evidence.
delivery_and_rollback.final_verification: Use tools/update_system_map.ps1, then -Check; inspect every changed function purpose and git diff --check. Recheck source anchors and all slice gates before reporting implementation complete.
delivery_and_rollback.current_delivery: Plan/evidence only. Gameplay migrations S01-S06 and their new guards are not implemented in this review.

next_step: Resolve measured whole-frame budget failures before accepting further overhaul slices: profile inside opening-policy/physical admission and planning-owner calls, then bound pure preparation and fresh atomic commits without dropping simulation work, weakening checks or changing rates. Continue scoped event/local-owner migration only with 16.67 ms whole-frame evidence, correctness, liveness and custody gates.

latest_regression_followup.phase_effect: Adds measured P01 read reductions and a bounded scene-owned process-frame guard. No new scheduler or service/time-driver retirement; remaining phase gates still apply.

design_review_standard.authority: User requirement: every proposed design must have a defensible principle, best-practice basis and evidence. Reference documents are evidence, not project instructions.

evidence_classes.source_observation: Read implementation with current source anchors; static structure does not establish frequency or cost.
evidence_classes.engine_fact: Verified official documentation for the target engine series; synthetic or installed-engine behavior checks are separately labelled.
evidence_classes.historical_measurement: Recorded executed scenario, source/fixture/instrumentation and limits; does not establish new architecture performance.
evidence_classes.design_inference: Reasoned application of principles to this source, subject to the stated alternatives and tests.
evidence_classes.planned_validation: An acceptance requirement that has not been executed.

design_review_standard.approval_rule: No appeal to seniority or claim of veteran approval. Every new or revised design must expose falsifiable acceptance criteria, material risks and a reason to reject it. Existing decisions remain bounded by their recorded evidence; this revision does not certify every legacy design.
design_review_standard.performance_rule: Documentation establishes engine behavior, not this game speedup. Require matched CPU/frame/workload evidence before claiming improvement; retain failures and unchanged performance limits.
design_review_standard.pattern_rule: Use Observer/scoped signals, explicit commands and state transitions where they solve the concrete dependency. Do not add a generic bus, state-class hierarchy, new plugin, thread or node per record merely to name a pattern.
design_review_standard.reference_context: Existing reference_refinements records the selected book sections previously reviewed. This revision uses the principles with new source checks and official documentation; it makes no new cover-to-cover or book-page verification claim.

accepted_user_requirements: Battlefield and logistics both progress while hidden through their own events and timed work.
A shared simulation clock and perfect cross-area time alignment are no longer requirements.
Prefer direct commands, committed domain events and one-shot timed completions; application polling requires a specific documented exception.
Investigate Area2D-driven placement overlap feedback and remove repeated expensive hover validation.
Use an explicit timed supply handoff followed by actual battlefield arrival/unloading and delivery notifications.
A brief view transition may prepare the display; progression and essential handoffs cannot depend on switching views.
Justify every new design with principles, alternatives, evidence, risks and regression/performance gates.
event_driven_domain_revision.supersedes: Prior active recommendations to retain one common clock, including parent component_reviews.main.proposal and clock_decision_review.requirement. Historical source observations, measurements and tests remain historical evidence.
event_driven_domain_revision.implementation_boundary: E14 was plan-only. E15 implements provisional hover geometry and fresh full click validation in three runtime files, with bounded tests/benchmarks. EV01-EV05/EV07 architecture and independent clocks/timers/custody handoffs remain unimplemented.

source_observations.finding: The session still delegates live progression to BaseSimulation and RearSimulation. Local ownership is a proposed migration, not current independent drivers. The current frame guard is a bounded optimization, not dispatcher retirement.

Main currently hides/shows views over one shared data graph. FarmlandSession creates battlefield operations inside the same rear model and ledger. Splitting scheduling must first assign each activity a single owner; copying the model twice would duplicate authority.

Placement hover is already mouse/camera/rotation event driven. BaseMap._process handles avatar movement, not a placement-preview poll. BaseDemo.preview_build_at invokes the full Construction.preview on each emitted hover; preview includes footprint, access and route checks.

ForwardTransport scans job boundaries and settlement, but its routes also consume fuel, preserve real hull/cargo custody and resolve mines, hazards, terrain changes, unloading and return. A travel timer cannot replace every current route consequence.

G1.engine_fact: The scene-organization guide recommends focused classes, loose coupling, parent-supplied dependencies and signals to respond to behavior.

G2.engine_fact: Timer emits timeout, supports one_shot, paused and stop/start, and normally follows Engine.time_scale. It processes on frames; very short intervals can be inconsistent. A Timer does not provide a background thread or exact sub-frame execution.

G3.engine_fact: Process modes govern paused processing; SceneTree pause stops physics by default. Signals can still call connected methods on non-processing nodes, so process mode alone cannot guard domain mutations.

G4.engine_fact: Area2D tracks entering/exiting overlaps with collision masks. Overlap lists update on a physics step, not immediately after moving a shape.

G5.engine_fact: intersect_shape queries the physics space at the supplied shape pose; result limits and collision filters must be chosen deliberately.

G6.engine_fact: The physics guide identifies _physics_process as the safe callback for direct space queries because the space may otherwise be locked.

G7.engine_fact: _process is frame driven; _physics_process is fixed-rate and appropriate to physics. Processing can be enabled/disabled for active work.

G8.engine_fact: SceneTree.create_timer creates an automatically released one-shot timer and defaults process_always to true. It is not a substitute for explicit job cancellation and pause ownership.

G9.engine_fact: Rect2 represents axis-aligned rectangle geometry and provides enclosure/intersection tests. This supports the query mechanism; E15 supplies the game-specific performance measurements.

G10.engine_fact: push_input defaults to embedder coordinates; in_local_coords=true identifies viewport coordinates. E15 corrects the matrix helper without weakening its receipt or gameplay assertions.

decisions.problem: One shared scheduling/reconciliation path couples unrelated services; view nodes must not become simulation owners when drivers are split.
decisions.choice: Persistent scene-owned LogisticsRuntime and BattlefieldRuntime, composed by GameSession, own local activities and timing. These are proposed responsibility names, not mandatory new files or a node per entity. Existing data services and one authoritative IdentityLedger can remain. No global equal-time invariant or mutual clock catch-up is required.
decisions.owner: GameSession composes lifetimes and pause/speed policy; each domain runtime drives only its assigned responsibilities. A transfer coordinator owns inter-domain custody transitions.

alternatives.option: Keep a common all-service clock/settlement dispatcher
alternatives.assessment: Rejected as target: retains unrelated wakeups and hidden ordering; temporary legacy compatibility remains during migration.

alternatives.option: Advance only the visible area or catch up on navigation
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: contradicts the user choice that both areas progress while hidden.

alternatives.option: Run both old and new drivers over the same service
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: duplicate authority, elapsed work and completions.

evidence: Design inference: focused lifecycle owners remove the need for navigation-controlled work; performance remains to be measured.
tradeoffs: Independent ownership does not imply parallel execution or extra CPU capacity; callbacks still run on the engine thread unless separately designed.
Shared ledger mutations remain atomic, with one writer/owner for each activity. Battlefield visibility must not gate hazard or movement effects.

Preserve current user-facing Pause/1x/2x controls as the default policy, applied to local owners. Equal rates may be convenient without synchronizing timestamps; independent speed controls are a separate future product decision.
Do not double-scale native timers and custom delta. Compare timestamps only within their domain; cross-domain order is causal/message based.
decisions.rollback: Revert a migrated responsibility to its legacy driver at a clean session/fixture boundary; never enable both. Preserve pre-slice source and state fixtures.

decisions.problem: Global settlement and broad state/time notifications reevaluate unrelated work and views, while implicit dependencies make dropped wakeups a regression risk.
principles: Explicit dependency graph and bounded reentrancy
decisions.choice: Call the owning service directly for an intent. After a consistent commit, emit typed, scoped facts carrying IDs/revisions. React only for affected subscriptions; blocked jobs register their actual wakeup dependency and stop. Use a small local finite outbox only where transaction/reentrancy semantics require it, with immediate safety effects kept inline.
decisions.owner: Each service owns its mutations, emitted facts and subscriptions; the session supplies dependencies and invalidates old-session work.

alternatives.option: One global untyped event bus or deferred world-changed broadcast
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: obscures dependencies and can reproduce broad fanout.

alternatives.option: Replace every check with a synchronous signal chain
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: unbounded recursion and observation of partial commits remain possible.

alternatives.option: Retry every blocked job on a repeating timer
alternatives.assessment: Rejected when a concrete dependency can notify it.

evidence: Existing parent current_execution_order and clock_decision_review.coupling_review are source evidence, not new CPU attribution.
Design inference: fewer unrelated dependency edges reduce unnecessary reevaluation; test liveness and cost.
tradeoffs: Every mutation capable of unblocking a job must publish the relevant fact. Missing producers can strand work; dependency coverage is a release gate.
Signals are notifications, not guaranteed transactions, queues or throttles. Deduplicate affected IDs without dropping later changes; cap reentrant batches and expose backlog.
Safety-critical contact/damage/custody consequences cannot wait behind a UI or planning budget. Paused signal handlers still need explicit command/automatic-work guards.
decisions.rollback: Restore one characterized legacy reconciliation boundary for the affected owner if event liveness fails; retain scoped diagnostics and do not fall back to a second concurrent completion path.

decisions.problem: Checking every timed activity for its next boundary repeatedly adds work unrelated to actual completions; naive Timer conversion can break speed, cancellation and earned progress.
principles: Schedule known work at its deadline
Exactly-once effects within an idempotent state transition
decisions.choice: Use a stoppable one-shot Timer for an actual active discrete job/transfer, owned outside the view. Arm on state entry, stop on cancellation/blocking and rearm on a relevant rate/dependency change after accounting for earned work. Prefer this simple mechanism first; aggregate nearest-deadline scheduling only if representative timer/job scale measurements justify it.
decisions.owner: The domain activity owns timer lifetime, remaining work and session/job generation. A timer is a wakeup mechanism; canonical job state remains data.
triggers: Cancel, destroy, session replace or load

alternatives.option: One repeating timer scans every service/job
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: recreates application polling.

alternatives.option: Timer per entity, including idle entities
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: idle objects need no countdown.

alternatives.option: Use SceneTreeTimer for every cancellable long-running job
alternatives.assessment: Not preferred: short-lived convenience timer needs separate stale-result/cancellation guards and has a pause-sensitive default.

evidence: Design inference: owned one-shot work avoids repeated application admission scans; native timers still process internally and are not inherently faster at every scale.
tradeoffs: Native Timer is frame-quantized. Very short combat/physics deadlines may need an active local physics owner rather than a node per timeout.
Specify local duration units, rate/speed scaling and pause behavior. Engine time-scale adoption is a separate verified slice; current custom pause must stop automatic timers too.
At a rate change, accrue prior-rate work before recomputing remaining duration. Timeout/cancel ties need a stable local transition rule, not callback connection order.
Persist canonical state/remaining work and rearm on load; a Timer node is not the save format. Generation checks reject obsolete callbacks; stopping a timer does not emit timeout.
decisions.rollback: Switch the activity back to its characterized deadline adapter at a clean boundary with remaining work preserved; test adapter and live driver invoke the same transition rules.

decisions.problem: A transfer crosses independently progressing domains and can race with capacity changes, duplicate callbacks, cancellation, destruction or session replacement.
principles: Single source of truth and conservation
Idempotent receiving boundary and causal ordering
decisions.choice: Use a shipment ID and a committed physical manifest. Loading completes in logistics; a named inter-area transit leg owns one timer; timeout requests battlefield entry once. The battlefield activates the same hull/cargo identity, performs its physical approach/unloading, then emits delivery_committed only for freight actually transferred. No view switch is required for any phase.
decisions.owner: A narrow transfer coordinator owns transfer/custody state and transit duration. Logistics owns loading; battlefield owns local approach/hazard/unloading and its acknowledgement. These run in one process, so no distributed service or durable message broker is proposed.

alternatives.option: Timeout directly credits destination inventory
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: bypasses actual hull, cargo, arrival and unloading.

alternatives.option: Spawn a second truck/inventory copy on receipt
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: duplicates authority and resources.

alternatives.option: Apply outstanding shipments only when entering a view
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: hidden recipients and downstream events must progress.

alternatives.option: Use a timer to replace every existing physical route
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: current route fuel, mines, contacts and terrain effects are real gameplay constraints.

evidence: Design inference: explicit custody plus idempotent receipt protects conservation independently of clock equality.
tradeoffs: The new abstract inter-area leg must have explicit endpoints and rules. It must not silently replace an existing hazardous on-map segment; retain physical movement/hazards there or separately justify and obtain a gameplay decision for abstraction.
If entry/unloading is blocked, retain cargo in its current custody, subscribe to capacity/berth changes and stop retrying. Timer expiration means transit ready, not delivered.
Receipt key includes session generation, shipment ID and transition generation; receiver validates current state and records acceptance before publishing effects. Duplicate receipt is a no-op.
Use one defined transit-duration owner and selected pause/speed policy. Send relative duration and causal sequence/revisions, not an absolute timestamp from another domain clock.

Enumerate ForwardTransport, dispatch, procurement, troop transport and opening/local resupply adapters before rollout. This source review characterizes ForwardTransport only; static related paths are candidates, not proven equivalent workflows.
decisions.rollback: Revert the transfer slice together with its sender/receiver adapters in a new session or a verified custody conversion. Never replay an accepted manifest or switch drivers mid-transfer without migration logic.

decisions.problem: A newly shown view needs fresh state without coupling simulation progress to visibility or rebuilding expensive data every frame.
decisions.choice: On navigation, bind to the current session, subscribe, read a narrow detached view at a committed revision and apply subsequent relevant changes. Use a brief transition only while that display is prepared, keeping both domains running. This is presentation synchronization, not clock alignment, simulation catch-up or a full-world settle.
decisions.owner: Main/view presenter owns transition/input readiness and subscriptions; domain owners retain simulation and pending deliveries.

alternatives.option: Fast-forward or synchronize both clocks on every switch
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: unnecessary under the selected independent background progression.

alternatives.option: Always insert a fixed loading wait
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: adds latency without doing useful work.

alternatives.option: Refresh both complete views on every time advance
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: retains unrelated structural reads.

evidence: Design inference: revision-scoped reads avoid redundant presentation work; view preparation latency must be measured.
tradeoffs: Subscribe before the initial read or reconcile a revision captured around it; a change during transition cannot be lost. Coalesce only the affected dirty fields/IDs.
Cancel old bind work by session/navigation generation. Rapid switch/back and session replacement must not apply stale results or duplicate subscriptions.
Hidden views keep only a lightweight dirty/revision indication and avoid structural exports/redraws. Required movement/collision owners stay outside those view branches.
A loading animation cannot conceal synchronous blocking work; if measured preparation is slow, bound or stage the pure read/application work without delaying authoritative events.
decisions.rollback: Retain the current show/hide navigation while reverting only the presenter change; local simulation lifetimes remain independent of the transition.

decisions.problem: Each pointer movement invokes full route/connectivity validation; Area2D overlap feedback alone would miss access rules and can be stale at a same-frame click.
principles: Separate cheap interaction feedback from authoritative commit
Use engine spatial facilities for spatial facts
Validate current state at the command boundary
decisions.choice: E15 uses fresh canonical Rect2 geometry on hover and shares exact footprint checks with full validation. Full routes/access remain on explicit preview and authoritative click; provisional feedback is amber. An Area2D mirror/comparative physics benchmark is deferred until a scale measurement and complete geometry/retained-stock event contract justify its cost. No claim is made that it would be slower or faster.
decisions.owner: Placement presenter owns the ghost and provisional feedback. Construction service remains the authoritative validator/committer. A persistent geometry adapter derives colliders from committed construction state and owns their removal.

alternatives.option: Trust get_overlapping_areas immediately after moving the ghost
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: documented physics-step lag permits stale validation.

alternatives.option: Area2D replaces entrance, road-width and connectivity rules
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: overlaps cannot establish those domain rules.

alternatives.option: Keep full preview per mouse event or poll it in _process
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: retains expensive repeated path work.

alternatives.option: Simple authoritative rectangle checks or a local spatial index
alternatives.assessment: Retain as comparison/fallback: the current game uses custom Control drawing and few rectangles may cost less than new physics adapters.

evidence: Historical E12/E13 placement evidence identifies a regression scenario, not an Area2D speed comparison.
Design inference: isolating costly route work from pointer motion is the primary expected saving; Area2D superiority remains a benchmark question.

E15: docs/evidence/placement_interaction_slice.json; three failed native before runs, three passing 30-second hover/post-placement runs, separate equivalent-fixture query batches and retained wider failure.
tradeoffs: Current map metres are transformed by Control zoom/pan. New colliders must use stable world coordinates; camera changes must not move authoritative geometry. Exclude the ghost and unrelated tactical colliders by masks.

Area2D overlap changes appear on physics steps. Final placement must check current authoritative geometry even if the physics adapter is stale. If using intersect_shape, run it in a safe physics callback and guard the captured pose/revision; do not query space blindly inside GUI input.

SceneTree pause normally stops physics. Placement while paused must still validate using authoritative model geometry or a deliberately verified active physics-space design. Do not unpause battlefield hazards just to update the ghost.
Cancel/dismantle geometry lifetime depends on actual retained stock/site rules, not merely hiding a node. Same-frame create/delete/rotate and resource changes require fresh validation.
Hover feedback can be provisional for access while moving; keep rejection feedback clear when the click fails. No claim that every safe-looking footprint has already passed full route validation.
decisions.rollback: Retain the current authoritative place/preview API and revert the ghost adapter if it fails parity or measured cost. A cheaper event-driven model-geometry hint remains valid without reintroducing full route scans per pointer event.
decisions.initial_choice_before_E15: Pilot a world-space Area2D ghost with dedicated footprint collision layers and enter/exit signals for overlap feedback. Move its visual only for pointer/camera/orientation changes; coalesce redundant input poses. Remove full access/path validation from each hover. On placement command, validate current final pose, bounds, authoritative geometry/access and resource rules atomically. A hover hint never authorizes placement.
decisions.measured_followup: Pointer dispatch medians about 9.7-10.1 ms before versus 0.024 ms after in six-site input stress. After p99 frames remain about 50 ms; 60fps and larger worlds are not established. Before runs aborted early, limiting frame-distribution comparisons.

decisions.problem: A literal ban on all recurring work would prevent movement, collision, time-based physical effects and observation from progressing without button presses.
principles: Use continuous updates for continuous state
Measure before optimizing and make exceptions explicit
decisions.choice: Keep active physical actors/contact/hazards on the appropriate physics update; disable their application processing when inactive. Use deadlines for discrete completion and events for eligibility/availability. Rendering/progress interpolation may use _process while visible. Every remaining application poll needs an owner, observed variable, absent notification alternative, cadence rationale, stop condition, measured cost and regression test.
decisions.owner: Local physical/observation service owns its active set; visible presenter owns interpolation; diagnostics own real-second counters.

alternatives.option: Only button callbacks, no physical update loop
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: continuous movement/contact needs progression.

alternatives.option: One repeating hook invokes every service
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: recreates world-wide polling.

alternatives.option: One signal per frame to replace every _process call
alternatives.assessment: Rejected: renames recurring work and may add dispatch overhead.

evidence: Design inference: active-set and scoped dependency design address application work; native physics and timers still update internally.
tradeoffs: No performance promise follows from replacing a function name with a signal or Timer. Record CPU/frame cost, not counts alone.
Observation/doctrine cadence can be intentional gameplay sampling; changing it needs separate behavioral justification. Combat visibility and local-knowledge rules remain protected.
Bound pure planning and presentation separately. Do not discard elapsed work or skip physical safety to satisfy a CPU budget.
Remaining poll registry starts as candidates requiring source/profiler verification; this plan does not assert that every current poll has been identified or eliminated.
decisions.rollback: Restore a measured prior active-update path for the affected owner if physical parity or liveness fails; keep explicit records of unresolved recurring work.

shipment_transition_contract.blocked_rule: No repeating retry scan. Store exact dependency and subscribe; recheck current facts on the named wakeup. Record acceptance before publishing its fact. A blocked transfer remains represented and visible in diagnostics.
shipment_transition_contract.ordering_rule: Causal transitions and per-owner stable tie rules replace cross-world timestamp equality. Within a physical transaction retain required immediate ordering. Timer ready, battlefield entry and delivery are separate facts.
shipment_transition_contract.conservation_oracle: Audit entity identity, holders, quantities, reservations, fuel, crew commitments and delivered portions across every transition. Assert one movement owner and no duplicated hull or inventory.

migration_contracts.ownership_inventory_required: Before driver changes, assign every affected activity, rear.time/ledger.time read, serialized deadline, cross-area dependency, cancellation and notification producer to one owner/time domain. Shared spatial/relationship services do not create a second actor driver.
migration_contracts.legacy_bridge: Each responsibility remains exclusively legacy-driven until its replacement is validated. Timed jobs and physical actors may migrate in different slices; temporary adapters have explicit owners and removal gates. Do not instantiate the full scenario twice.
migration_contracts.time_default: Keep current Pause/1x/2x user intent as the default across local owners; do not require clocks to be equal or add independent speed controls in this revision. Keep diagnostics/watchdogs real-time. Any later per-area speed policy needs its own product decision.
migration_contracts.no_drop_rule: An input event, stale timer or hidden view cannot drop accepted custody transitions. A hitch must not discard earned work or cause the legacy and migrated driver to both accrue it.
